title: Guru Gobind Singh: sword and saint
hookLine: the tenth Guru's light: the Khalsa, the song, the courage
tomorrow: after ten Gurus, who is the Guru now?

cards: Simran started her morning with the Ardas, standing in the kitchen, her own small asks folded inside it.

Then she went to the dispatch desk and saw it again: the newest driver, whose English is still shaky, gets the worst routes every week, the long hauls and the late loads. Nobody says anything. She prayed first.
Then what does she do? She asks her dad for five minutes, and she brings the route sheets.

teach.b: Pray, then act bravely: that's the tenth Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, in one line.

Tradition says that on Vaisakhi at Anandpur he called for volunteers ready to give their heads, and from the Five Beloved who stood up, the Khalsa began: saint-soldiers, sant sipahi, the prayer and the courage in one body.
He was a poet too, and his verse is full of this pairing.
In Chandi Charitra, in paraphrase: grant me this, that I never turn back from doing good, and never fear the enemy when I go to face it.
And in the Zafarnama, his letter to the emperor Aurangzeb, he sets the order: when every other way has failed, it is right to take up the sword.
The sword comes last, after words, after patience.
Here's one to tell a friend tonight: the Guru who founded the Khalsa wrote that the sword comes last. For Simran, the sword is a stack of route sheets and a steady voice.
Harjit listens, frowns at the sheets, and says: not your business. Simran doesn't argue. She leaves the sheets on his desk.

how: Sikhs celebrate the birth of the Khalsa at Vaisakhi and Guru Gobind Singh's birth at his gurpurab; initiated Sikhs of the Khalsa wear the five Ks, and his compositions such as the Jaap are part of the daily prayers.

o: a Mughal emperor who later protected the Sikhs
the Guru who first wrote the Sikh evening prayer
the tenth Guru, saint and soldier, who founded the Khalsa

games.q: the tenth Guru — tap the pairs.
p: never turn back from doing good
the sword only when all else fails

s: the Khalsa was founded so Sikhs could start wars
saint-soldiers: prayer and courage together, with the sword as the last tool.
Guru Gobind Singh was a poet as well as a leader
Chandi Charitra and the Zafarnama are both his verse.
in the Zafarnama, the sword is the first answer to injustice
only when every other way has failed.

games.q: a friend says a younger kid is being shaken down for lunch money behind the gym. you pray about it. what's the sword-and-saint next step?
o: keep praying; the saint's part is enough if your heart is right.
go confront the older kids yourself; the sword is for the helpless.
tell an adult you trust what you heard; words before anything sharper.
games.why: pray, then act bravely, in order: words first. the Zafarnama keeps the sword for when every other way has failed.

practice: Bring to mind one wrong near you that people keep walking past: at school, at work, at home. Name what's in the way of saying something: fear, awkwardness, not knowing how.
Then plan the first brave step, the calm words first, and say the opening sentence quietly to yourself.

wordCard.voice: Guru Gobind Singh: the tenth Guru, saint and soldier. He made the Khalsa, wrote the song, and put the sword last.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: sant sipahi, saint-soldier; the ideal of the Khalsa.

carryVoice: Words for today: sword and saint, the prayer first and then the brave act. Words before anything sharper.
